##1. Architecture Overview | Component | Where it lives | What it does | How it talks to the other pieces | |-----------|----------------|--------------|-----------------------------------| | **`EventRecorder` interface** | `staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/internal/events/interfaces.go` | Minimal contract used by any component that wants to publish a **Kubernetes Event** (the same contract used by the core `k8s.io/client-go/tools/events` package). | Implementations are injected by the Cilium agent via the **Hive** DI container. The drop‑event emitter receives an implementation of this interface and calls it whenever it wants to raise a warning about a dropped packet. | | **Drop‑event emitter** | `pkg/hubble/dropeventemitter/dropeventemitter.go` (core logic)
`pkg/hubble/dropeventemitter/cell.go` (Hive wiring) | Listens to Hubble flow records, filters for **packet‑drop** events that were caused by a Cilium network‑policy, builds a human‑readable message and forwards it to the `EventRecorder`. | The emitter is registered as a **Hubble flow processor** (`flow.Processor`). The processor receives a `flowpb.Flow` from the Hubble observer, extracts the drop reason, looks‑up the policy that caused it and finally calls `recorder.Eventf(...)`. | | **Hive cell that provides the recorder** | `pkg/kube/kclient/events.go` (thin wrapper that builds a concrete recorder from the client‑go `eventBroadcaster`) | Creates a concrete implementation of `EventRecorder` that talks to the Kubernetes API server (creates `Event` objects in the `default` namespace). | The cell is part of the **Cilium agent** DI graph; when the agent starts it creates a `Broadcaster`, a `Recorder` and registers the recorder as a dependency for the drop‑event emitter cell. | | **Kubernetes API server** | External to the repo | Persists the `Event` objects created by the recorder; they become visible via `kubectl get events` or the UI. | The recorder uses the standard client‑go `corev1.EventInterface` to POST the event. | **Data path for a dropped packet** 1. **Ingress/Egress packet** → eBPF datapath → **Drop event** is written to the perf‑event map. 2. **Hubble observer** reads the perf‑event map, decodes it into a `flowpb.Flow`. 3. The **drop‑event emitter** receives the flow, checks `flow.GetDropReason()` and the policy that caused it. 4. It builds a message like *“Packet dropped by policy (L4: TCP, src 10.0.0.5:12345 → dst 10.0.0.10:80)”* and calls `recorder.Eventf(...)`. 5. The concrete recorder talks to the **Kubernetes API server**, which stores the `Event` object. --- ## 2. Detailed Analysis ### 2.1 The `EventRecorder` interface (current definition) ```go // staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/internal/events/interfaces.go package events import ( "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime" ) // EventRecorder is the minimal contract used by Cilium to emit a warning event. // It deliberately mirrors the subset of the upstream client-go interface that // Cilium needs (the full client-go interface also has Event, Eventf, PastEventf, …). type EventRecorder interface { // Eventf records a formatted event. The implementation creates a // corev1.Event object with type "Warning". Eventf(object runtime.Object, eventtype, reason, action, note string, args ...interface{}) } ``` *The file is deliberately tiny – it only contains the `Eventf` method that Cilium’s drop‑event emitter uses.* ### 2.2 Why a new method is required The **drop‑event emitter** (`pkg/hubble/dropeventemitter/dropeventemitter.go`) currently calls: ```go recorder.Eventf(endpoint, corev1.EventTypeWarning, "PacketDrop", "Drop", msg, args...) ``` The new feature (as requested) wants the emitter to also include **the list of policies that contributed to the drop** in the event *reason* field, which the upstream `EventRecorder` does **not** expose. The easiest way is to add a new method that accepts a slice of policy names: ```go // New method to be added RecordDrop(object runtime.Object, policies []string, msg string, args ...interface{}) ``` The implementation will simply join the policy names and forward to `Eventf` (or directly create a `corev1.Event` if we want richer fields). ### 2.3 Files that must be changed | Repo | File | Reason for change | |------|------|-------------------| | **cilium** (the main repo) | `staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/internal/events/interfaces.go` | Add the new method signature to the `EventRecorder` interface. | | **cilium** | `pkg/kube/kclient/events.go` | Provide a concrete implementation that satisfies the extended interface (wrap the existing recorder and implement `RecordDrop`). | | **cilium** | `pkg/hubble/dropeventemitter/dropeventemitter.go` | Change the emitter to call the new `RecordDrop` method instead of `Eventf`. | | **cilium** | `pkg/hubble/dropeventemitter/cell.go` | Update the cell wiring to inject the extended recorder (no code change needed if the concrete type implements the new method). | | **cilium** (optional) | Any unit‑test that builds a fake recorder (e.g., `pkg/controller/test/recorder.go`, `pkg/test/eventrecorder.go`) | Extend the fake implementations so they also implement `RecordDrop`. | ### 2.4 Exact code changes (diff‑style) #### 2.4.1 `staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/internal/events/interfaces.go` ```diff @@ type EventRecorder interface { // Eventf records a formatted event. The implementation creates a // corev1.Event object with type "Warning". - Eventf(object runtime.Object, eventtype, reason, action, note string, args ...interface{}) + Eventf(object runtime.Object, eventtype, reason, action, note string, args ...interface{}) + + // RecordDrop records a packet‑drop event together with the list of + // policies that caused the drop. The concrete implementation may + // embed the policy list in the event's Reason field or in the + // Message (note) field – the contract only guarantees that the + // information is persisted in the resulting corev1.Event. + // + // `policies` may be nil or empty; in that case the call behaves + // like Eventf with a generic reason. + RecordDrop(object runtime.Object, policies []string, note string, args ...interface{}) } ``` #### 2.4.2 `pkg/kube/kclient/events.go` (concrete implementation) ```diff @@ type recorder struct { broadcaster record.EventBroadcaster recorder record.EventRecorder } func (r *recorder) Eventf(obj runtime.Object, eventtype, reason, action, note string, args ...interface{}) { r.recorder.Eventf(obj, eventtype, reason, action, note, args...) } +// RecordDrop implements the new method. It joins the policy names into a +// single string and forwards everything to the underlying recorder. +func (r *recorder) RecordDrop(obj runtime.Object, policies []string, note string, args ...interface{}) { + // If we have policies, embed them in the reason field so they are + // searchable via `kubectl get events -o wide`. + reason := "PacketDrop" + if len(policies) > 0 { + reason = fmt.Sprintf("PacketDrop[%s]", strings.Join(policies, ",")) + } + r.recorder.Eventf(obj, corev1.EventTypeWarning, reason, "Drop", note, args...) +} ``` *(imports `fmt` and `strings` are added at the top of the file.)* #### 2.4.3 `pkg/hubble/dropeventemitter/dropeventemitter.go` ```diff @@ func (e *dropEventEmitter) ProcessFlow(ctx context.Context, flow *flowpb.Flow) { @@ - // Old behaviour – only a generic warning. - e.recorder.Eventf(endpoint, corev1.EventTypeWarning, - "PacketDrop", "Drop", msg, args...) + // New behaviour – include the policies that caused the drop. + e.recorder.RecordDrop(endpoint, policyNames, msg, args...) } ``` *`policyNames` is a `[]string` built earlier in the function from the `flow.GetPolicyMatch()` field.* #### 2.4.4 Fake recorder used in tests (`pkg/controller/test/recorder.go`) ```diff @@ type FakeRecorder struct { Events []corev1.Event } -func (f *FakeRecorder) Eventf(obj runtime.Object, eventtype, reason, action, note string, args ...interface{}) { +func (f *FakeRecorder) Eventf(obj runtime.Object, eventtype, reason, action, note string, args ...interface{}) { // existing logic … } +func (f *FakeRecorder) RecordDrop(obj runtime.Object, policies []string, note string, args ...interface{}) { + // Re‑use Eventf – embed policies in the reason. + reason := "PacketDrop" + if len(policies) > 0 { + reason = fmt.Sprintf("PacketDrop[%s]", strings.Join(policies, ",")) + } + f.Eventf(obj, corev1.EventTypeWarning, reason, "Drop", note, args...) +} ``` #### 2.4.5 `pkg/hubble/dropeventemitter/cell.go` No code change is required because the cell injects a `events.EventRecorder`; the concrete type now implements the extra method automatically. ### 2.5 Dependency graph impact ``` [Hive] → recorder cell → concrete recorder (implements EventRecorder + RecordDrop) ↓ [dropEventEmitter cell] → dropEventEmitter (uses EventRecorder) ↓ [Hubble flow observer] → ProcessFlow → RecordDrop → Kubernetes API ``` Only the **recorder** and **drop‑event emitter** need to be re‑compiled; all other components that depend on `EventRecorder` continue to work because the original `Eventf` method is still present. ### 2.6 Build & Test verification | Step | Command | Expected outcome | |------|---------|-------------------| | 1. Pull the repository (already done) | `git checkout ` | Working tree with the files listed above | | 2. Apply the patches (the diffs shown) | `git apply ` | Files updated | | 3. Run `go test ./...` from the repository root | `make test` (or `go test ./...`) | All existing unit tests pass; new fake recorder compiles | | 4. Build the Cilium agent binary | `make cilium-agent` | Binary builds without “does not implement EventRecorder” errors | | 5. Run a quick integration test (if available) that exercises Hubble → drop‑event emitter | `make integration-test` | The emitted events now contain the policy list in the Reason field | If any test fails because a mock recorder does not implement the new method, add the stub as shown in **2.4.4**. --- ## 3. Relevant Files (complete list) | Repo (knowledgeId) | File Path | Why it matters | |--------------------|-----------|-----------------| | `ab057f46-1b78-43c7-84b3-bc98fd2c5101` (Cilium) | `staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/internal/events/interfaces.go` | Defines the `EventRecorder` interface – the place where the new method is added. | | `ab057f46-1b78-43c7-84b3-bc98fd2c5101` | `pkg/kube/kclient/events.go` | Concrete implementation that satisfies the extended interface; adds the `RecordDrop` method. | | `ab057f46-1b78-43c7-84b3-bc98fd2c5101` | `pkg/hubble/dropeventemitter/dropeventemitter.go` | Core drop‑event emitter that now calls `RecordDrop` instead of `Eventf`. | | `ab057f46-1b78-43c7-84b3-bc98fd2c5101` | `pkg/hubble/dropeventemitter/cell.go` | Hive wiring – unchanged but re‑uses the same dependency. | | `ab057f46-1b78-43c7-84b3-bc98fd2c5101` | `pkg/controller/test/recorder.go` | Fake recorder used by unit tests; extended to implement `RecordDrop`. | | `ab057f46-1b78-43c7-84b3-bc98fd2c5101` | `pkg/test/eventrecorder.go` (Karpenter) – *not compiled by Cilium* | Example of another fake recorder; not required for Cilium but shown for completeness. | | `ab057f46-1b78-43c7-84b3-bc98fd2c5101` | `pkg/kube/kclient/events.go` (wrapper that creates the recorder) | The place where the recorder is instantiated and injected into the Hive graph. | | `ab057f46-1b78-43c7-84b3-bc98fd2c5101` | `pkg/hubble/dropeventemitter/dropeventemitter_test.go` | Unit test that validates the emitter’s behaviour – will now verify that the `Reason` field contains the policy list. | *(All files belong to the **Cilium** repository – the only repo that contains the `EventRecorder` interface used by the drop‑event emitter.)* --- ### TL;DR * Add `RecordDrop(object runtime.Object, policies []string, note string, args ...interface{})` to `staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/internal/events/interfaces.go`. * Implement the method in the concrete recorder (`pkg/kube/kclient/events.go`) – join the policy slice into a reason string
